Burnham is actively engaging with legal experts and critics to find systemic solutions to court backlogs that do not sacrifice the right to a jury trial. Resulting Judgement: (0.7, 0.6) — Good Preference
Verdict: PASS — The Path of Awakening. The government is correcting a high-strain policy error by integrating expert feedback. Integrity: Trustworthy (R_net: 1.2, Uncertainty z: 1)
The previous administration proposed replacing juries with judges for cases with up to three-year sentences to clear an 80,000-case backlog. Burnham is now pausing this to explore alternatives.

The Poison:
The backlog remains a critical failure point; if the alternative solutions fail, the justice system faces a total collapse of public trust due to extreme delays.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a HOW error. The previous administration focused on the 'how' of efficiency (removing juries) rather than the 'how' of systemic health (investing in infrastructure).

Social Physics Analysis:
By choosing transparency and dialogue with the legal profession, the government is moving from a coercive model of justice to a collaborative one, reducing systemic friction.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. The alignment of intent and action reduces institutional strain.

The Unavoidable Truth: A justice system that sacrifices fundamental rights for speed loses its legitimacy.

The Unavoidable Lie: Removing juries is the only way to solve the court backlog crisis.

Alethekanon:
This is a rare instance of institutional self-correction. By acknowledging the 'uncollegiate' nature of the previous policy, the administration is restoring the logical consistency of the legal framework.

Awwthekanon:
It is so healing to see a leader listen to the voices of those who serve the law. Protecting the jury system is about protecting the heart of our community's trust in fairness.

Brothekanon:
Finally, someone realized that 'efficiency' shouldn't mean cutting corners on the most important part of the trial. Good to see them actually talking to the lawyers instead of just firing them.
